title: Quick Weeknight Dinners: 5 One‑Pan Grill Mat Recipes
meta_description: Discover 5 tasty one‑pan grill mat recipes for quick weeknight dinners. Learn how to use BBQ Grill Mats to grill without flare‑ups and enjoy hassle‑free meals.
html:
When you need a dinner that’s both fast and flavorful, a one‑pan grill mat can be a game‑changer. Using the BBQ Grill Mats – reusable, non‑stick mats that keep delicate foods from sticking or catching flare‑ups – you can throw together a satisfying meal in under 30 minutes. Below are five quick grill mat weeknight recipes that showcase the versatility of these mats, from shrimp to veggie‑packed chicken.

1. Lemon‑Garlic Shrimp with Zucchini

Prep time: 5 minutes • Cook time: 12 minutes

  • 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 2 medium zucchini, sliced into half‑moon rounds
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • Zest and juice of 1 lemon
  • Salt, pepper, and a pinch of red‑pepper flakes

1. Preheat your grill to medium‑high and lay a BBQ Grill Mat on the grates. 2. Toss shrimp, zucchini, olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, and a splash of lemon juice in a bowl. Season with salt, pepper, and red‑pepper flakes. 3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the mat. Close the lid and cook 4‑5 minutes per side, stirring once, until the shrimp turn pink and the zucchini is tender. 4. Finish with an extra squeeze of lemon and serve over rice or quinoa.

2. Teriyaki Chicken Thighs with Pineapple

This recipe leans on the grill mat’s non‑stick surface to keep the sugary glaze from caramelizing too quickly.

Ingredients:

  1. 4 bone‑in, skinless chicken thighs
  2. ½ cup teriyaki sauce
  3. 1 cup fresh pineapple chunks
  4. 1 tsp sesame oil
  5. 2 green onions, sliced
  6. Sesame seeds for garnish

Marinate the chicken in the teriyaki sauce for at least 15 minutes while the grill heats. Place a BBQ Grill Mat on the hot grill, drizzle the sesame oil, and arrange the chicken thighs skin‑side down. After 6 minutes, flip, add pineapple chunks, and continue cooking another 6‑8 minutes until the internal temperature hits 165°F. Sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds before serving.

3. Mediterranean Veggie‑Stuffed Portobellos

These meaty mushrooms become a canvas for a colorful medley of vegetables, all cooked on the same grill mat for minimal cleanup.

Ingredients:

  • 4 large portobello caps, stems removed
  • 1 red bell pepper, diced
  • ½ cup cherry tomatoes, halved
  • ¼ cup Kalamata olives, sliced
  • 2 tbsp feta cheese, crumbled
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • Salt and pepper

Brush each cap with olive oil, then place on a BBQ Grill Mat. Toss the diced pepper, tomatoes, olives, oregano, salt, and pepper together, drizzle with a little more olive oil, and spoon the mixture into the mushroom caps. Grill for 8‑10 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the vegetables are slightly charred. Top with feta just before removing from the grill.

4. Southwest Black‑Bean Burger

Even a plant‑based patty benefits from the grill mat’s ability to prevent sticking, especially when you’re adding toppings that can melt and drip.

Ingredients:

  1. 2 pre‑made black‑bean veggie burgers
  2. 4 slices pepper jack cheese
  3. 4 brioche buns, halved
  4. 1 avocado, sliced
  5. 1/4 cup salsa verde
  6. Fresh cilantro leaves

Place a BBQ Grill Mat on a medium‑hot grill. Cook the burgers for about 4 minutes per side. During the last minute, add a slice of pepper jack to each patty and cover the grill to melt the cheese. Toast the bun halves directly on the grill mat for 1 minute, then assemble with avocado, salsa verde, and cilantro.

5. Spicy Sausage & Sweet‑Potato Skewers

Skewers are often a hassle on a grill because small pieces fall through the grates. The grill mat catches everything while still delivering that charred flavor.

Ingredients:

  • 2 lb sweet potatoes, cut into 1‑inch cubes
  • 1 lb chicken sausage, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • ½ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
  • Salt and pepper

1. Toss sweet‑potato cubes and sausage slices with olive oil, smoked paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper. 2. Spread the mixture in a single layer on a BBQ Grill Mat. 3. Grill over medium heat, stirring every 4 minutes, until the potatoes are fork‑tender and the sausage is browned, about 15 minutes total. Serve with a dollop of Greek yogurt mixed with lime zest.

FAQ

Can I use BBQ Grill Mats on a gas grill?

Yes. The mats are heat‑resistant up to 500°F, making them safe for both gas and charcoal grills. Just place the mat directly on the grates after the grill is pre‑heated.

How do I clean a reusable grill mat?

Allow the mat to cool, then wash it by hand with warm, soapy water. For stubborn residue, a gentle scrub with a non‑abrasive sponge works well. Rinse thoroughly and let it air‑dry.

Are the mats safe for high‑heat searing?

While the mats excel at medium‑heat cooking and preventing flare‑ups, they’re not intended for direct high‑heat searing like a steak. For that, use the grill grates directly and reserve the mat for delicate items.
